Last Friday (21st) was the sentencing of the Hong Kong Alliance case. In the early morning, police took a woman who was queuing to attend the hearing onto a police vehicle. In response to enquiries, the police said the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty" and "seditious intent".

At around 5 a.m. last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During the queue, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue was "suspected of having clothing with seditious intent", and took her onto a police vehicle. When officers took the woman away, several officers kept directing journalists to leave, saying "take you to the press area", and pulled the orange cordon line towards the direction of Ying Wa Street. After the woman boarded the police vehicle, the cordon was removed. A "court-watching volunteer" who was queuing near the woman said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

"The Collective" enquired with the police about the reasons for the woman being taken away and whether the police had made an arrest. The police replied this morning (24th) that on August 21, a security operation was conducted in the area of the West Kowloon Courts, during which a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty" and "seditious intent", and was detained for investigation.
